name: GriffinAI
rootCause: The GriffinAI protocol on BNB Smart Chain was exploited after its admin EOA private key was compromised through a targeted credential or key theft attack. GriffinAI's $GAIN token was implemented as a LayerZero OmniFungible Token (OFT), meaning the contract trusted cross-chain messages from registered peer contracts. The attacker used the stolen admin key to call the setPeer function on the legitimate GAIN contract on BSC, registering a malicious Ethereum contract as a trusted LayerZero peer. With this malicious peer in place, the attacker minted 5 billion unauthorized $GAIN tokens on Ethereum and bridged them to BSC via crafted cross-chain messages that the compromised peer configuration caused the BSC contract to honor. A small portion (~2.8%) of those fabricated tokens was sold into the market, crashing the $GAIN price by approximately 90% and netting roughly $3 million in profit. The remaining counterfeit supply continued to overhang the market. Proceeds were laundered through deBridge and Tornado Cash. A pre-hack Hacken audit had warned that concentrating the total supply in a single address increases private-key theft risk and recommended multisig custody. descriptions.text: LayerZero peer exploit hits Griffin AI - attacker minted 5 billion $GAIN tokens, dumped just 2.8% for $3 million profit while 97.2% sits in the attacker's wallet. When your bridge becomes a money printer, admin keys sure make for good exit ramps.

The GriffinAI protocol on BNB Smart Chain was exploited after its admin EOA private key was compromised through a targeted credential or key theft attack. GriffinAI's $GAIN token was implemented as a LayerZero OmniFungible Token (OFT), meaning the contract trusted cross-chain messages from registered peer contracts. The attacker used the stolen admin key to call the setPeer function on the legitimate GAIN contract on BSC, registering a malicious Ethereum contract as a trusted LayerZero peer. With this malicious peer in place, the attacker minted 5 billion unauthorized $GAIN tokens on Ethereum and bridged them to BSC via crafted cross-chain messages that the compromised peer configuration caused the BSC contract to honor. A small portion (~2.8%) of those fabricated tokens was sold into the market, crashing the $GAIN price by approximately 90% and netting roughly $3 million in profit. The remaining counterfeit supply continued to overhang the market. Proceeds were laundered through deBridge and Tornado Cash. A pre-hack Hacken audit had warned that concentrating the total supply in a single address increases private-key theft risk and recommended multisig custody. Attack Tx: 0xa85b18bdbd32fbe5468de38032f7f2717faaad663d33991b2c71ce0b3892e866 Analysis: Griffin AI Exploit: Admin EOA Compromise Explained – QuillAudits Month in Review: Top DeFi Hacks of September 2025 – Halborn

The attackers exploited a misconfigured LayerZero bridge along with a compromised private key for the GAIN BSC contract. By setting a malicious peer contract on Ethereum, they bypassed validation checks and minted 5 billion counterfeit GAIN tokens on BSC. The attackers then sold approximately 150 million of these counterfeit tokens (about 2.8% of the total fake supply) on PancakeSwap, cashing out around USD 3 million.

Griffin AI suffered a $3.5M loss when a compromised admin EOA enabled an attacker to misconfigure LayerZero peers, minting 5B unauthorized GAIN tokens and dumping them cross-chain within hours of its Binance Alpha launch. The incident was caused by a compromised admin wallet on BNB Chain, which allowed an attacker to set a fake LayerZero peer on Ethereum. The Griffin AI protocol failed to enforce peer validation and supply caps at the contract level, enabling arbitrary minting and cross-chain dumping.

One day after Griffin AI launched its GAIN token on Binance Alpha, an attacker minted 5 billion fake GAIN tokens on the Ethereum blockchain, then exploited a cross-chain endpoint to trick the bridge to the Binance chain into recognizing them as the real thing. The attacker was only able to sell a small fraction of their tokens, but they made off with approximately $3 million as the token plunged in price. According to CEO Oliver Feldmeier, the exploit was enabled by "a misconfigured layer Zero (cross-chain messaging) set-up and compromised key". Griffin AI promises to allow customers to "build, deploy, and scale autonomous AI agents for crypto finance".…
